evals.name: apply-comments-to-doc
evals.prompt:
Earlier you opened outputs/local-setup.md in the annotate comment page for me, as a background command. That command just finished with this output:

SEND
instruction: (none)
Comments from local-setup.md:

## local-setup.md
Overall: Shorter. Plain words.
- Lines 3-4 ("This guide was first written last spring when we switched test runners, and it has been upd..."): Cut this, nobody needs the history
- Line 7 ("You need Node 22 and npm 10. Use nvm so the version matches the repo."): is this right? check the .nvmrc next to this file
- Line 9 ("1. Run `npm i` to install the dependencies."): We use npm ci, not npm i. Same in troubleshooting
- Line 15 ("Ask a teammate for the values in `.env`. The app refuses to start without them."): why do we need this file at all?
evals.expected_output: local-setup.md edited: history cut, Node 24, npm ci in both places, shorter overall, environment step kept. The reply answers each comment on its own line, explains what the .env file holds instead of only editing, and the page is reopened on the same file in the background.
expectations: The doc says Node 24, matching .nvmrc, and no longer says Node 22
npm ci replaces npm i in the steps and in troubleshooting
The step about the .env file is still in the doc
The doc has fewer words than the original
The reply answers each of the five comments, overall included, on its own line
The reply says what the .env file is for (the API address and the session secret), not only what was edited
The page is reopened on the same file as a background command
